r25q_34c61d43d1c6a0f0c7.explanation: The Arjun Hale over-31 review is the Hale-Lane delivery, identical to its pavilion-end entry, the 13:34 folio-45 review and the signed scorer sheet at folio 45 row 9. The striker's-end umpire signalled Wide and the bowler's-end umpire signalled No ball, so under Law 21.12 the No-ball overrides the Wide and the delivery status is NO_BALL. No completed runs or boundary are recorded, so Laws 21.14-21.15 yield one No-ball extra, zero batter runs, one bowler run, and the ball does not count in the over (Law 21.16). Counterfactual: removing the No-ball signal leaves the Wide standing (initial call set WIDE_ONLY), so the delivery is a Wide worth one Wide extra, zero batter runs, one bowler run, and it does not count in the over (Law 22.8); contact, running, boundary allowance and source selections are unchanged.

r25q_3d0a7bcd3ac8a03ace.explanation: The match-control index resolves the Kyle Rowe over-37 review to the Rowe-Shaw delivery; all observations attach to that delivery only. The audio log records no No-ball signal and no Wide is recorded, so the initial call set is NONE and the delivery is legal. The ball touched the striker's bat and then broke the wicket, which Law 32.1 accepts for Bowled; the fielding side appealed and the appeal preceded the next run-up and Time, satisfying Laws 31.1/31.3, and the wicket event was submitted as Bowled. No completed runs or boundary are recorded, so all accounts are zero and the legal ball counts in the over. Counterfactual: adding a bowler's-end No-ball call makes the delivery a No-ball (Law 21.12; no competing Wide), which under Law 21.17 removes Bowled (leaving dismissal NONE), adds one No-ball extra under Laws 21.14-21.15 (credited to the bowler with no batter runs), and the ball does not count in the over (Law 21.16); contact, running, boundary and lock/source selections are unchanged.

r25q_7685b11e2ad222c6db.explanation: The Carter Lane over-16 review is the Lane-Ford delivery, identical to its pavilion-end entry. The striker's-end umpire signalled Wide and the ball touched neither bat nor person, so under Law 22.3.1 the Wide stands and the delivery status is WIDE. The boundary came directly from the delivery (not an overthrow) with the agreed allowance of 4; because there was no bat contact, the 4-run boundary plus the 1-run Wide penalty are recorded as Wides (Laws 22.6-22.7), giving 5 Wide extras, zero batter runs, and 5 bowler runs; the Wide does not count as one of the over (Law 22.8). No completed running is recorded before the boundary. Counterfactual: with bat contact, Law 22.3.1 revokes the Wide; the delivery becomes legal, the 4-run boundary is credited to the striker as batter runs (Laws 19.6-19.7 with the agreed 4-run allowance), bowler runs equal the 4 batter runs, and the ball counts in the over; the initial Wide call, running, boundary allowance and source selections are unchanged.
